text:
sasha: Heads up — observed an admin session to the private control plane from an IP outside the Dedicated VPC allowlist. looks like the session used the onprem-admin role.
sec-bot: [alert] Unusual admin login detected (rule: private-vpc-allowlist). generated ticket INC-2026-0034.
matt: Can you paste the raw event and the conn metadata? need ip, source, and the role claim.
sasha: pasted logs below:
```
ts=2026-03-18T21:42:03Z event=websocket_connect user=svc-bastion role=onprem-admin src_ip=52.48.112.17 dest=private-controlplane.redwood svc_token=ephemeral-xxxx
audit: session_id=abc123 auth_method=impersonation principal=svc-bastion impersonated=onprem-admin
kms: no decrypt entry found for session_id=abc123
```
leena: hmm KMS decrypt missing is weird — either the SDK call used caching or the audit sink didn't include CloudKMS. when the RBAC refactor ran last week did we change any KMS iam bindings?
adrian: yes — the last RBAC patch unified onprem and dedicated admin mappings so service-account impersonation got a new rolebinding. PR: https://github.com/redwood/platform/pull/819
judy: if an allowlist bypass happened we should revoke the session and rotate the ephemeral tokens for that service account. can someone run revoke_tokens for svc-bastion?
matt: running now: `./scripts/revoke_tokens --service-account svc-bastion --session abc123` -> done. reported TTLs revoked, session dropped.
sasha: confirmed session disconnected. but we still need root cause: why KMS audit missing and how the connection got through the vpc check.
leena: two hypotheses:
- policy routing bug: controlplane accepted connections proxied through our external bastion; allowlist check looked at internal hop ip instead of origin ip
- role mapping regression: onprem-admin got a short-circuit allow rule during refactor
adrian: I recall adding a compatibility rule to fall back to legacy allowlist for onprem roles; that might be too permissive. I'll grep the RBAC config and revert the fallback on the controlplane policy.
sec-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0034, severity=high, responders=[matt,leena,adrian], slack-thread=2401234567
matt: I'll collect forensic artifacts: controlplane access logs (last 24h), bastion proxy headers, and kube-audit for impersonation events.
leena: I'll check KMS audit export (CloudAuditLogs) for that key's decrypt entries and confirm key policy bindings. if audit export shows a gap, escalate to infra for exported log retention.
judy: I'll open a hotfix PR to tighten the allowlist check to use X-Forwarded-For and require origin IP in the dedicated VPC range. PR: https://github.com/redwood/controlplane/pull/1022
sasha: PR opened and started a canary deny rule for onprem-admin on one controlplane node.
adrian: quick note — if the canary denies legitimate automation, revert immediately. keep sec informed.
matt: forensic snapshot uploaded to s3://forensics/INC-2026-0034/; added a checklist:
- confirm origin IP -> done
- check role mapping diffs -> todo
- verify KMS audit -> todo
leena: if KMS audit is actually missing, propose rotating the key with a new key version and re-encrypting critical secrets as precaution.
judy: will draft customer-facing blurb in case this impacts private deployments — mark as internal for now.
sasha: summary/todo:
- adrian: revert permissive fallback in RBAC policy (in progress)
- judy: hotfix PR to strict XFF origin check (PR #1022)
- matt: collect logs + maintain forensic artifacts
- leena: validate KMS audit export and IAM bindings
- sec-bot: incident open INC-2026-0034
we'll sync in 30m in #eng-security and keep updates here. :white_check_mark:
